records.issue_text: [BUG] Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() converts the cached-adapter NPE into a silent null contract violation that will NPE at unboxing sites. Any caller treating the result as a primitive long (e.g., admin console/REST count endpoints that unbox the Long) now throws a NullPointerException downstream instead of getting a stale-but-valid count; the fix trades a server-side cache race for a client-visible NPE with no error semantics.
records.rationale: In GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount(), the diff changes behavior from always returning a non-null Long (via getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount()) to potentially returning null when modelSupplier.get() is null (`return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`). This introduces a new null return path that can cause downstream NullPointerException when callers unbox to primitive long or otherwise assume non-null, matching the finding’s mechanism.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The reader thread is never joined and exceptions raised after deletedAll.set(true) are lost, so the assertion can pass even when the race it claims to cover actually fires. The test is flaky-by-design: the background thread keeps looping only until the flag flips, an exception thrown in the final iteration (or during the in-flight request) is recorded after assertThat runs, so a genuine regression in this exact fix passes CI — missing verification for the bug being fixed.
records.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the background reader thread is started with `new Thread(() -> { while (!deletedAll.get()) { ... } }).start();` but the `Thread` is never retained or `join()`ed. After deleting groups, the test immediately does `deletedAll.set(true);` and then `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty());`. This allows (a) the reader thread to still be in-flight when the assertion runs and (b) exceptions to be added to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion, making the test able to pass even if the concurrent read actually fails.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] fail() is called inside the IntStream lambda but the loop continues creating groups and the test does not abort on first failure, mixing assertion semantics with partial setup. A later contributor debugging this test sees a confusing mix of created and failed groups; failure attribution is per-group rather than per-test, making diagnosis of CI failures harder.
records.rationale: The diff shows `fail("Failed to create group...")` is called in the `else` branch inside `IntStream.range(...).forEach(...)` with **no surrounding try/catch** to swallow the thrown error: `} else { fail("Failed to create group: " + ...); }`. Since `fail(...)` throws an exception, it will abort the stream/test at the first failure rather than “continuing creating groups,” contradicting the finding’s core claim.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() replaces the NPE with a null Long that downstream callers unbox or aggregate, so the same race now surfaces as an NPE elsewhere (e.g. in the resource provider summing counts) instead of being handled as a retry/re-fetch. When a group is deleted concurrently, callers that do `long count = adapter.getSubGroupsCount()` or `mapToLong` on the stream get a NullPointerException at a site further from the cause; the contract of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() is a non-null Long, and this diff silently widens it to nullable for only this one implementer while every other implementer still returns non-null, so callers cannot defensively code for it.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Adding @Override to getRealm() implies a change in an interface/supertype contract (the method now overrides something new), and no corresponding change to that interface or its other implementers appears in this diff — if the interface method was added or its signature changed, out-of-tree implementers of the cached-entity contract silently stop overriding it and drift from the new contract. Custom/experimental implementations of the cache-entity interface (e.g. alternate cache stores in downstream forks) compile unchanged but no longer satisfy the new contract, and a rename or signature change in the parent becomes a silent behavioral break rather than a compile error.
records.rationale: The diff only adds an `@Override` annotation to an existing `getRealm()` method in `CachedGroup` (`+    @Override` before `public String getRealm()`), with no signature change and no shown change to any interface/supertype. Adding `@Override` does not itself imply a new/changed contract; it only enforces at compile time that the method already overrides something. The finding’s premise (that this implies an interface/supertype contract change) is not supported by the diff.
